Kept at 4096. The cap was never the thing sending heredocs to `create_file`. Below the cap a heredoc always ran through `run_bash`, and it does on master too: a 433-character `cat > /tmp/report.md << 'EOF'` returns `None` from master's `_check_bash_command`. The `create_file` message only explains why an over-cap command was rejected, so raising the cap moves where that message starts and keeps it. The two steering tests build their input from `_BASH_MAX_LENGTH` so they keep testing that over-cap branch, and they fail if it stops naming `create_file`.

#1969 asks to raise the cap but gives no number. 4096 fits a typical heredoc or chained one-liner with room to spare. If you would rather use 2048, that is a one-line change and I will make it.

discussion_comments.comment_body:
Yes, that is intended. Heredocs between 513 and 4096 characters now run through `run_bash`. #1969 asks for that: the 512 cap was refusing normal work for its length. Above 4096 the same `create_file` message still fires.

The two steering tests were not changed to drop an assertion. Their fixed inputs (833 and 1292 characters) cross 512 but not 4096, so at the new cap they would no longer reach the branch they test. They now build their input from `_BASH_MAX_LENGTH`, so they keep testing the over-cap message at whatever the cap is. If you want a smaller cap, it is a one-line change.
